# Adjudication Task — Chapter 55

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃55화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|‘환장하겠네.’
  6|
  7|혁무진은 눈앞이 노래지는 것을 느꼈다.
  8|
  9|중소 문파의 제자들로 위장하고 있던 암살자들. 그리고 대장로의 배신. 여기까지만 해도 머리가 터질 지경인데…….
 10|
 11|‘이 인간은 왜 쓰러진 거냐고!’
 12|
 13|난데없이 진태경이 정신을 잃었다. 정찰조원들이 돌아가며 뺨도 때리고, 멱살을 짤짤 흔들어도 깨어날 기미가 안 보인다.
 14|
 15|‘분명히 숨은 붙어 있는데.’
 16|
 17|귀신이 곡할 노릇이다. 일이 이렇게 되니 결국 부조장인 자신이 이 엄청난 일의 책임자가 되어 버렸다.
 18|
 19|“너, 그리고 너.”
 20|
 21|아직도 혼란에 빠져 있는 정찰조원들 중 두 사람을 지목한 혁무진이 말했다.
 22|
 23|“너희 둘은 지금 당장 본가로 복귀해서 이 사실을 알려라.”
 24|
 25|대장로.
 26|
 27|가문의 웃어른이자 옛 정마대전의 영웅인 그가 어떤 이유로, 무엇을 위해 이런 암계를 꾸몄는지는 모른다.
 28|
 29|그러나 최악의 사태만은 막아야 했다.
 30|
 31|“나머지는 모두 본대로 이동한다. 서둘러!”
 32|
 33|혁무진은 정신을 잃고 쓰러져 있는 진태경을 등에 업었다.
 34|
 35|그렇게 한 시진 가량을 달리자 이번에는 다른 의미로 눈앞이 노래졌다.
 36|
 37|‘죽겠네.’
 38|
 39|조필의 무지막지한 일장(一掌)에 내상을 입었던 것이 불과 며칠 전이다. 진태경에게는 거의 다 나았다고 큰소리를 쳤지만 사실 보름은 꼼짝없이 요양해야 할 상태였다.
 40|
 41|“헉, 허억.”
 42|
 43|온몸이 흠뻑 젖고 다리가 후들거린다.
 44|
 45|그냥 따라가도 뒤처질 판인데 건장한 체구의 진태경까지 업고 있으니 그야말로 죽을 지경이다.
 46|
 47|‘아, 어머니. 아버지.’
 48|
 49|이제는 멀쩡히 살아 계신 부모님이 손짓하는 환영까지 보인다. 두 분 옆에 선 아주머니는 법당에서 자주 본 얼굴이다.
 50|
 51|‘관음보살님?’
 52|
 53|- 중생아. 고생했다. 이제 쉬어도 좋다.
 54|
 55|자애로운 미소에 혁무진의 마음이 스르륵 풀어졌다.
 56|
 57|그래, 이 정도면 할 만큼 했지. 조장이라는 인간은 정작 중요할 때 픽 쓰러지고. 조원이라는 새끼들은 내가 죽든 말든 대신 업겠다는 소리도 안 하고.
 58|
 59|‘시벌, 모르겠다.’
 60|
 61|혁무진이 정신을 놓으려던 그때였다.
 62|
 63|“후우, 하아아.”
 64|
 65|귓구멍을 파고드는 따뜻한 숨결. 누구인지는 돌아보지 않아도 알 수 있었다. 혁무진은 반가움에 눈물이 핑 돌았다.
 66|
 67|“조장!”
 68|
 69|진태경이 씩 웃으며 속삭였다.
 70|
 71|“네 귀에 캔디.”
 72|
 73|
 74|
 75|* * *
 76|
 77|
 78|
 79|챙! 채챙!
 80|
 81|“죽여! 죽여!”
 82|
 83|“크아악!”
 84|
 85|곳곳에서 피와 비명이 터져 나온다. 피를 뒤집어쓴 무인이 시체 사이를 엉금엉금 기어간다.
 86|
 87|아직 앳된 얼굴이 고통과 공포로 얼룩져 있었다.
 88|
 89|“흐윽, 흐으윽.”
 90|
 91|참으려 해도 터져 나오는 울음. 십 년을 절치부심하며 무공을 익혔지만 피 튀기는 전장에서는 무소용이었다.
 92|
 93|든든하던 선배가, 형제 같던 동기가 죽었다. 사방에서 쏟아진 병장기가 배를 가르고 사지를 난도질했다.
 94|
 95|“어머니, 어머니…….”
 96|
 97|하염없이 어머니를 부르던 그의 얼굴이 딱딱하게 굳었다.
 98|
 99|푹-!
100|
101|어느새 가슴팍에 돋아난 창날. 순간 부릅떠진 눈동자에서 이내 빛이 사라진다. 산적처럼 수염이 난 낭인이 녹슨 창을 뽑아내며 씩 웃었다.
102|
103|“애새끼가 어딜.”
104|
105|하지만 수없이 죽을 고비를 넘긴 낭인도, 다음 순간 날아드는 칼날을 피할 수는 없었다.
106|
107|서걱-
108|
109|은빛 선과 함께 낭인의 목이 솟구쳤다. 무인을 죽인 낭인, 낭인을 죽인 또 다른 무인.
110|
111|이름도 모르는 이들이 사방에서 죽고 죽이기를 반복했다.
112|
113|전장(戰場)은 그런 곳이었다.
114|
115|‘그래, 이런 곳이었지.’
116|
117|대장로는 상념에 젖은 얼굴로 전장을 바라봤다.
118|
119|팔천협(八天峽). 수십 년 전 정마대전의 한 줄을 장식했던 격전지. 저 비좁은 협곡에서 얼마나 많은 이들이 죽어 갔던가.
120|
121|‘그때는 나도 젊었지.’
122|
123|육체는 강인했고 가슴은 뜨거웠다. 협(俠)이라는 낯간지러운 글자가 크게 느껴지던 시절이었다.
124|
125|그러나 정마대전을 겪으며 대장로는 변했다. 끝없이 이어지는 전쟁에 지쳤고 죽음이 두려워졌다.
126|
127|‘협의지사가 무슨 소용인가. 죽으면 귀신에 불과한 것을.’
128|
129|그건 한 줄기 깨달음이었다. 마침내 그는 살아남아 영웅이 되었고, 기나긴 인고의 시간 끝에 이 자리에 섰다.
130|
131|이제 결실을 맺어야 할 때. 대장로는 노회한 눈으로 옆에 선 한 사람을 응시했다.
132|
133|‘아깝구나. 아까워.’
134|
135|진위경은 뛰어난 인재다. 젊고, 무공도 상당하며 무엇보다 지도자에게 필요한 위엄과 판단력을 지녔다. 간혹 정에 얽매이는 모습을 보이긴 했지만 그 덕인지 가문 내에서 인망도 두터웠다.
136|
137|‘능히 본가를 일으킬 수 있는 재목이다.’
138|
139|만약 진위경이 태원진가의 가주가 된다면. 그리고 각기 두각을 나타내고 있는 두 아우가 뒤를 든든히 받쳐 준다면…….
140|
141|대장로는 문득 자신의 생각을 깨닫고 피식 웃었다.
142|
143|여기까지 온 마당에 이 무슨 해괴한 짓거리란 말인가. 심지어 진태경은 이미 죽어 고혼이 되었을 텐데.
144|
145|“나도 늙었군.”
146|
147|작은 중얼거림에 진위경이 반응했다.
148|
149|“뭐라 하셨습니까?”
150|
151|“별것 아니오. 원래 늙으면 혼잣말이 늘거든. 그보다 소가주가 보기에는 어떻소?”
152|
153|“전황은 유리하게 흘러가고 있습니다만…….”
154|
155|진위경의 표정이 살짝 어두워졌다. 병력의 질과 지형에서 우위를 점하고 있다고는 하나 피해는 꾸준히 누적되고 있었다.
156|
157|가솔들의 죽음을 바라보는 그의 마음이 편할 리 없다.
158|
159|“소가주. 그 마음은 알지만 경거망동하지 마시오.”
160|
161|대장로는 엄중한 어조로 충고했다.
162|
163|“우두머리는 나설 때를 알아야 하는 법, 전투가 길어질수록 조급해지는 것은 놈들이니 그때를 노려야 하오.”
164|
165|“곧 항산검문에서도 총력으로 부딪쳐 오겠군요.”
166|
167|“절정 고수들을 앞세우겠지. 문주인 이천백이 직접 올 수도 있고.”
168|
169|“그때 모든 게 결정 나겠군요.”
170|
171|대장로가 고개를 끄덕였다.
172|
173|“소가주와 나, 위팽이 적들의 수뇌부를 막고 절벽 위에서 화살비가 쏟아지면 사기가 바닥으로 떨어질 거요.”
174|
175|“화공을 못 쓰는 것이 아쉽습니다. 하늘이 원망스럽군요.”
176|
177|팔천협의 좁은 지형은 화공에 안성맞춤이지만 며칠 전 내린 폭설로 인해 사방이 눈 더미였다.
178|
179|그러나 하늘이 그의 편을 들어 주었다 해도 진위경이 기대하는 일은 일어나지 않았을 것이다.
180|
181|절벽 위에서 활시위를 당길 이들은 대장로의 명령을 따를 테니까.
182|
183|“나도 하늘이 원망스럽소.”
184|
185|대장로의 말은 진심이었다.
186|
187|기다린 세월이 너무 길었다. 이제야 찾아온 천명이 원망스러웠다.
188|
189|
190|
191|* * *
192|
193|
194|
195|“네 귀에 캔디.”
196|
197|“조장!”
198|
199|“꿈처럼 달콤했니.”
200|
201|“……미쳤어요?”
202|
203|못생긴 혁무진의 얼굴을 보자 반가움이 솟구쳤다. 내가 깨어났다는 말에 몰려든 다른 정찰조원들도 마찬가지였다.
204|
205|“조장님 깨어나셨다!”
206|
207|“무슨 일입니까? 몸은 괜찮으세요?”
208|
209|“죽은 거 아니었어?”
210|
211|방금 말한 새끼는 나중에 손봐 줘야겠다. 나는 얼굴과 이름을 기억해 둔 다음 모두에게 씩 웃어 보였다.
212|
213|“오랜만이네. 잘들 있었냐?”
214|
215|“예?”
216|
217|“그게 무슨 말이래?”
218|
219|“혹시 머리 다치신 거 아냐?”
220|
221|“머리, 머리를 보자!”
222|
223|충분히 예상했던 반응이다. 하지만 진심으로 한 번쯤 하고 싶었던 인사이기도 했다.
224|
225|……미친놈 취급 받았지만.
226|
227|“뭐 인사는 여기까지 하고. 나 기절한 지 얼마나 됐어?”
228|
229|혁무진이 털썩 주저앉으며 대답했다.
230|
231|“반 시진은 확실히 넘었고, 한 시진은 좀 안 됐을 겁니다.”
232|
233|현실에서 2주를 보냈으니 얼추 시간이 맞아떨어진다. 나는 고개를 끄덕이고 다음 질문으로 넘어갔다.
234|
235|“나 숨은 쉬었냐?”
236|
237|“갑자기 왜 그래요, 진짜?”
238|
239|“시간 없다. 빨리 대답해.”
240|
241|“숨 쉬고 있었으니까 일어나신 거죠. 아니면 죽었게요?”
242|
243|그것도 그러네.
244|
245|로그인, 혹은 로그아웃 시 다른 한쪽은 가사 상태에 빠지는 모양이다.
246|
247|‘암살자들 처리하기 전에 로그아웃했으면 돌아올 몸도 없었겠군.’
248|
249|이 부분은 나중에 생각하기로 하자.
250|
251|당장 급한 문제는 따로 있다.
252|
253|“본대는?”
254|
255|“안 그래도 그쪽으로 이동 중이었습니다. 두 명은 따로 빼서 가문으로 돌려보냈고요.”
256|
257|“잘했어. 거리는 얼마나 남았지?”
258|
259|“적어도 한 시진은 더 걸릴 것 같습니다.”
260|
261|“한 시진이라.”
262|
263|“저, 조장. 이런 말씀 드려서 죄송하지만…… 최악의 경우도 생각해야 할 것 같습니다.”
264|
265|혁무진은 물론이고 정찰조원들 모두가 입을 꾹 다물었다. 최악의 경우가 뭘 뜻하는지 모르는 사람은 아무도 없었다.
266|
267|‘나도 생각해 봤고.’
268|
269|곽준이 죽기 직전 했던 말에 따르면 이번 배신은 오래전부터 철두철미하게 계획된 것이다.
270|
271|하지만 그 계획엔 딱 한 가지 오류가 있다.
272|
273|‘바로 나.’
274|
275|대장로는 나를 너무 과소평가했다. 아니, 한편으로는 과대평가일지도 모르겠다. 자그마치 일류 고수 수십 명을 붙여 나를 죽이려고 했으니까.
276|
277|그러나 그것만으로는 역부족이었고, 나는 살아남았다.
278|
279|‘실수한 거지.’
280|
281|거기에 더해, 곽준은 처음 본색을 드러내며 그런 말도 했다. 슬슬 움직여야 시간에 맞출 수 있다고.
282|
283|그러니까…….
284|
285|“아직 안 늦었어.”
286|
287|조원들 한 명, 한 명과 시선을 맞추며 단호하게 말했다.
288|
289|“최악의 경우는 생각하지 마라. 무슨 수를 써서라도 내가 그 결과를 바꿀 테니까.”
290|
291|“조장…….”
292|
293|“그러니까 무진아.”
294|
295|나는 울컥한 표정의 혁무진에게 사람 좋게 웃어 보였다.
296|
297|“당장 일어나.”
298|
299|“힘들어 죽겠습니다.”
300|
301|“맞아 죽고 싶냐?”
302|
303|“…….”
304|
305|“이 시간에 한 걸음이라도 더 뛰렴. 마라톤 정신 몰라?”
306|
307|“모르는데요.”
308|
309|아. 여기 무림이지.
310|
311|“아무튼 빨리 일어나. 반 시진만 더 가면 된다.”
312|
313|후들거리는 다리를 부여잡고 일어나던 혁무진이 고개를 갸웃한다.
314|
315|“반 시진이요?”
316|
317|“응, 반 시진.”
318|
319|“말씀드렸잖아요. 최대한 빨리 가도 한 시진이라니까요.”
320|
321|“그러니까. 반 시진.”
322|
323|“지금 무슨 말씀을 하시는…….”
324|
325|“무진아.”
326|
327|“예?”
328|
329|소처럼 순박하게 눈을 끔뻑이는 혁무진에게, 나는 더더욱 환하게 웃어 보였다.
330|
331|“근성이라는 말, 들어 봤냐?”
332|
333|한 시진이든 두 시진이든 상관없다.
334|

He called for her over and over until his face suddenly went rigid.

[P47]
Shunk—!

[P48]
A spearhead protruded from his chest.

[P49]
His eyes flew wide for an instant, then the light faded from them. A wandering martial artist with a bandit’s beard pulled his rusty spear free and grinned.

[P50]
“What’s a brat doing here?”

[P51]
But even a wanderer who had survived countless brushes with death could not dodge the blade that came flying at him the next moment.

[P52]
Slice—

[P53]
A silver line flashed, and the wanderer’s head flew into the air.

[P54]
A wanderer killed a martial artist, only for another martial artist to kill him.

[P55]
Nameless men killed and died on every side, over and over.

[P56]
That was what a battlefield was.

[P57]
*Yes. This was what it was like.*

[P58]
The Head Elder gazed over the battlefield, lost in memory.

[P59]
Eight Spring Gorge. A battleground that had earned a single line in the history of the Great Faction War decades ago. How many people had died in that narrow gorge?

[P60]
*I was young then, too.*

[P61]
His body had been strong, and his heart had burned hot. Back then, the embarrassing word *chivalry* had still meant so much to him.

[P62]
But the Great Faction War had changed the Head Elder. He had grown weary of the endless fighting and afraid of death.

[P63]
*What good is being a chivalrous hero? Once you die, you’re nothing but a ghost.*

[P64]
That realization had been a form of enlightenment. In the end, he had survived and become a hero. After long years of patient endurance, he had finally reached this point.

[P65]
Now it was time to reap the fruit.

[P66]
The Head Elder turned his shrewd old eyes toward the man standing beside him.

[P67]
*What a waste. Such a waste.*

[P68]
Jin Wikyung was a remarkable talent. He was young, highly accomplished in martial arts, and above all, possessed the dignity and judgment a leader needed. He sometimes allowed sentiment to sway him, but perhaps that was also why he was so deeply respected within the family.

[P69]
*He is more than capable of restoring this family.*

[P70]
If Jin Wikyung became the Family Head, and if his two younger brothers—each already distinguishing himself—stood firmly behind him…

[P71]
The Head Elder caught himself and let out a short laugh.

[P72]
What a ridiculous thing to be thinking after coming this far. Besides, Jin Taekyung was probably already dead, reduced to a lonely ghost.

[P73]
“I’ve grown old.”

[P74]
Jin Wikyung reacted to the quiet mutter.

[P75]
“Did you say something?”

[P76]
“Nothing of importance. Old men tend to talk to themselves. More importantly, how does the battle look to you, Lesser Family Head?”

[P77]
“It is going in our favor, but…”

[P78]
Jin Wikyung’s expression darkened slightly. They held the advantage in troop quality and terrain, but their casualties continued to mount.

[P79]
There was no way he could watch members of his family die and feel at ease.

[P80]
“Lesser Family Head. I understand how you feel, but do not act rashly.”

[P81]
The Head Elder’s warning was stern.

[P82]
“A leader must know when to step forward. The longer the battle drags on, the more impatient the enemy will become. That is the moment we must seize.”

[P83]
“The Mount Heng Sword Sect will soon throw its full strength at us.”

[P84]
“They’ll put their Peak masters at the front. Their Sect Leader, Lee Cheonbaek, may even come himself.”

[P85]
“Then everything will be decided.”

[P86]
The Head Elder nodded.

[P87]
“If you, Wipeng, and I hold off the enemy commanders while arrows rain down from the cliffs, their morale will collapse.”

[P88]
“It’s a shame we can’t use fire. I resent the heavens.”

[P89]
The narrow terrain of Eight Spring Gorge was perfect for a fire attack, but the heavy snowfall several days ago had left snowdrifts everywhere.

[P90]
Yet even if the heavens had taken Jin Wikyung’s side, what he hoped for would never have happened.

[P91]
The men drawing their bows atop the cliffs would obey the Head Elder’s command.

[P92]
“I resent the heavens as well.”

[P93]
The Head Elder meant it.

[P94]
He had waited far too many years. He resented Heaven’s mandate for arriving only now.

[P95]
* * *

[P96]
“Candy in your ear.”

[P97]
“Captain!”

[P98]
“Was it sweet as a dream?”

[P99]
“…Are you insane?”

[P100]
The sight of Hyuk Mujin’s ugly face filled me with relief. I felt the same way about the other reconnaissance squad members who crowded around after hearing I was awake.

[P101]
“Captain’s awake!”

[P102]
“What happened? Are you all right?”

[P103]
“Wasn’t he dead?”

[P104]
I’d have to deal with the bastard who had just said that later. I memorized his face and name, then grinned at everyone.

[P105]
“Been a while. You guys been well?”

[P106]
“Huh?”

[P107]
“What’s that supposed to mean?”

[P108]
“Did he hit his head?”

[P109]
“His head—check his head!”

[P110]
Exactly the reaction I’d expected.

[P111]
Still, it was a greeting I’d genuinely wanted to give them at least once.

[P112]
…Even if it made them treat me like a lunatic.

[P113]
“Anyway, that’s enough greetings. How long was I out?”

[P114]
Mujin dropped to the ground with a thud and answered.

[P115]
“Definitely more than an hour, but probably a little under two.”

[P116]
I’d spent two weeks in reality, so the timing roughly lined up. I nodded and moved on to my next question.

[P117]
“Was I breathing?”

[P118]
“Why are you asking that all of a sudden? Seriously.”

[P119]
“We don’t have time. Just answer.”

[P120]
“You were breathing, so you woke up. Otherwise, you’d be dead.”

[P121]
Fair enough.

[P122]
Apparently, logging in or out left my body on the other side in a state of suspended animation.

[P123]
*If I’d logged out before dealing with the assassins, there wouldn’t have been a body left for me to return to.*

[P124]
I’d think about that later.

[P125]
There was a more urgent problem.

[P126]
“The main force?”

[P127]
“We were already heading toward them. I split off two men and sent them back to the family.”

[P128]
“Good. How much farther?”

[P129]
“At least another two hours.”

[P130]
“Two hours…”

[P131]
“Uh, Captain. I’m sorry to say this, but… I think we have to consider the worst-case scenario.”

[P132]
Mujin and every member of the reconnaissance squad fell silent. Nobody had to ask what the worst-case scenario meant.

[P133]
*I’ve thought about it too.*

[P134]
According to what Gwak Jun had said just before he died, this betrayal had been meticulously planned for a long time.

[P135]
But the plan had exactly one flaw.

[P136]
*Me.*

[P137]
The Head Elder had underestimated me.

[P138]
No—maybe in a way, he had overestimated me. He’d sent dozens of First Rate masters just to kill me.

[P139]
Even that hadn’t been enough. I had survived.

[P140]
*He made a mistake.*

[P141]
On top of that, when Gwak Jun first revealed his true colors, he’d said they needed to get moving soon if they wanted to arrive on time.

[P142]
Which meant…

[P143]
“It’s not too late.”

[P144]
I met each squad member’s eyes and spoke firmly.

[P145]
“Don’t think about the worst-case scenario. No matter what it takes, I’ll change that outcome.”

[P146]
“Captain…”

[P147]
“So, Mujin.”

[P148]
I gave Mujin’s choked-up face a good-natured smile.

[P149]
“Get up. Now.”

[P150]
“I’m dying here.”

[P151]
“Want to get beaten to death instead?”

[P152]
“…”

[P153]
“Run one more step while we still have time. Don’t you know the marathon spirit?”

[P154]
“I don’t.”

[P155]
Ah. Right. This was Murim.

[P156]
“Anyway, get up. Another hour will do it.”

[P157]
Mujin grabbed his trembling legs and forced himself upright, then cocked his head.

[P158]
“An hour?”

[P159]
“Yeah. An hour.”

[P160]
“I already told you. Even at full speed, it’ll take two hours.”

[P161]
“Exactly. An hour.”

[P162]
“What are you even talking about…?”

[P163]
“Mujin.”

[P164]
“Yes?”

[P165]
Mujin blinked at me with the guileless eyes of an ox. I smiled even brighter.

[P166]
“You ever heard of grit?”

[P167]
I didn’t care whether it should take two hours or four.

[P168]
We were getting there in one hour. Period.

[P169]
“Run like hell. That’ll do it.”

[P170]
“Huk.”

[P171]
Every face in the reconnaissance squad went deathly pale.

[P172]
* * *

[P173]
“We’ve been blocked.”

[P174]
“Casualties are mounting. Sect Leader, please take action.”

[P175]
Even as the reports continued, Blood Wolf Sword Lee Cheonbaek, Sect Leader of the Mount Heng Sword Sect, did not open his eyes.

[P176]
*I was too hasty.*

[P177]
The war had begun in a rush, and their preparations had been just as inadequate. Provisions were rapidly running out, morale was falling, and more men were deserting by the hour.

[P178]
*They saw through everything.*

[P179]
Rage over his son’s death and impatience with the situation had clouded his judgment. He had ignored his subordinates’ advice and chosen the fastest route.

[P180]
And so he had encountered the Jin Family of Taiyuan in a narrow gorge whose very name had been unfamiliar to him: Eight Spring Gorge.

[P181]
“Sect Leader!”

[P182]
At his subordinate’s shout, Lee Cheonbaek slowly opened his eyes.

[P183]
The formidable eyesight of a Peak master pierced the battlefield.

[P184]
“Gaaah!”

[P185]
“Wipe them out! They’re nothing but rabble!”

[P186]
Well over a thousand of his men were trapped at the narrow entrance, unable to advance. The wandering martial artists and mounted bandits he had placed at the front had numbers, but individually, they were inferior even to the Jin Family’s rank-and-file warriors.

[P187]
*Sword fodder, at best.*

[P188]
Just as he clicked his tongue inwardly, several dozen wandering martial artists began peeling away from the front line. The middle-aged wanderer leading them shouted at the top of his lungs.

[P189]
“This is a dog’s death! Brothers of the Blood Rain Group, fall back!”

[P190]
Those became his last words.

[P191]
Whoosh—

[P192]
A light breeze.

[P193]
That was all the wanderer felt.

[P194]
He did not realize that Blood Wolf Sword Lee Cheonbaek had already swept past him, nor did he see his men freeze in terror.

[P195]
He only thought, all of a sudden, that his neck felt hot.

[P196]
“Uh…”

[P197]
His cleanly severed head dropped to the ground. The headless body staggered several more steps before collapsing like a rotten old tree.

[P198]
“Blood Rain Group, was it?”

[P199]
Lee Cheonbaek pointed his sword at the frozen wanderers. Not a single drop of blood stained the blade.

[P200]
“Go back.”

[P201]
A Peak master’s killing intent struck them like a blade. The wandering martial artists charged back toward the front even faster than they had fled.

[P202]
They had decided that fighting on the front line was preferable to challenging the Peak master before them.

[P203]
“Rats.”

[P204]
Lee Cheonbaek followed them. His blazing gaze was fixed somewhere ahead, where the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s commanders had to be.

[P205]
“The Sect Leader is taking the lead!”

[P206]
“Everyone, charge! Wipe out the Jin Family of Taiyuan!”

[P207]
As Lee Cheonbaek stepped forward, the Mount Heng Sword Sect’s core forces followed.

[P208]
Three Peak masters and dozens of First Rate masters surged toward the front.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

His still-youthful face was twisted with pain and terror.

[P42]
“Hnnh… hhhk…”

[P43]
He tried to hold it back, but the sobs kept breaking free. He had spent ten years gritting his teeth and honing his martial arts, yet none of it had helped him on this blood-soaked battlefield.

[P44]
The senior he had relied on was dead. So was the fellow disciple who had been like a brother. Weapons had poured in from every direction, splitting open bellies and hacking limbs apart.

[P45]
“Mother… Mother…”

[P46]
He called for her over and over until his face suddenly went rigid.

[P47]
Shunk—!

[P48]
A spearhead protruded from his chest.

[P49]
His eyes flew wide for an instant, then the light faded from them. A wandering martial artist with a bandit’s beard pulled his rusty spear free and grinned.

[P50]
“What’s a brat doing here?”

[P51]
But even a wanderer who had survived countless brushes with death could not dodge the blade that came flying at him the next moment.

[P52]
Slice—

[P53]
A silver line flashed, and the wanderer’s head flew into the air.

[P54]
A wanderer killed a martial artist, only for another martial artist to kill him.

[P55]
Nameless men killed and died on every side, over and over.

[P56]
That was what a battlefield was.

[P57]
*Yes. This was what it was like.*

[P58]
The Head Elder gazed over the battlefield, lost in memory.

[P59]
Eight Spring Gorge. A battleground that had earned a single line in the history of the Great Faction War decades ago. How many people had died in that narrow gorge?

[P60]
*I was young then, too.*

[P61]
His body had been strong, and his heart had burned hot. Back then, the embarrassing word *chivalry* had still meant so much to him.

[P62]
But the Great Faction War had changed the Head Elder. He had grown weary of the endless fighting and afraid of death.

[P63]
*What good is being a chivalrous hero? Once you die, you’re nothing but a ghost.*

[P64]
That realization had been a form of enlightenment. In the end, he had survived and become a hero. After long years of patient endurance, he had finally reached this point.

[P65]
Now it was time to reap the fruit.

[P66]
The Head Elder turned his shrewd old eyes toward the man standing beside him.

[P67]
*What a waste. Such a waste.*

[P68]
Jin Wikyung was a remarkable talent. He was young, highly accomplished in martial arts, and above all, possessed the dignity and judgment a leader needed. He sometimes allowed sentiment to sway him, but perhaps that was also why he was so deeply respected within the family.

[P69]
*He is more than capable of restoring this family.*

[P70]
If Jin Wikyung became the Family Head, and if his two younger brothers—each already distinguishing himself—stood firmly behind him…

[P71]
The Head Elder caught himself and let out a short laugh.

[P72]
What a ridiculous thing to be thinking after coming this far. Besides, Jin Taekyung was probably already dead, reduced to a lonely ghost.

[P73]
“I’ve grown old.”

[P74]
Jin Wikyung reacted to the quiet mutter.

[P75]
“Did you say something?”

[P76]
“Nothing of importance. Old men tend to talk to themselves. More importantly, how does the battle look to you, Lesser Family Head?”

[P77]
“It is going in our favor, but…”

[P78]
Jin Wikyung’s expression darkened slightly. They held the advantage in troop quality and terrain, but their casualties continued to mount.

[P79]
There was no way he could watch members of his family die and feel at ease.

[P80]
“Lesser Family Head. I understand how you feel, but do not act rashly.”

[P81]
The Head Elder’s warning was stern.

[P82]
“A leader must know when to step forward. The longer the battle drags on, the more impatient the enemy will become. That is the moment we must seize.”

[P83]
“The Mount Heng Sword Sect will soon throw its full strength at us.”

[P84]
“They’ll put their Peak masters at the front. Their Sect Leader, Lee Cheonbaek, may even come himself.”

[P85]
“Then everything will be decided.”

[P86]
The Head Elder nodded.

[P87]
“If you, Wipeng, and I hold off the enemy commanders while arrows rain down from the cliffs, their morale will collapse.”

[P88]
“It’s a shame we can’t use fire. I resent the heavens.”

[P89]
The narrow terrain of Eight Spring Gorge was perfect for a fire attack, but the heavy snowfall several days ago had left snowdrifts everywhere.

[P90]
Yet even if the heavens had taken Jin Wikyung’s side, what he hoped for would never have happened.

[P91]
The men drawing their bows atop the cliffs would obey the Head Elder’s command.

[P92]
“I resent the heavens as well.”

[P93]
The Head Elder meant it.

[P94]
He had waited far too many years. He resented Heaven’s mandate for arriving only now.

[P95]
* * *

[P96]
“Candy in your ear.”

[P97]
“Captain!”

[P98]
“Was it sweet as a dream?”

[P99]
“…Are you insane?”

[P100]
The sight of Hyuk Mujin’s ugly face filled me with relief. I felt the same way about the other reconnaissance squad members who crowded around after hearing I was awake.

[P101]
“Captain’s awake!”

[P102]
“What happened? Are you all right?”

[P103]
“Wasn’t he dead?”

[P104]
I’d have to deal with the bastard who had just said that later. I memorized his face and name, then grinned at everyone.

[P105]
“Been a while. You guys been well?”

[P106]
“Huh?”

[P107]
“What’s that supposed to mean?”

[P108]
“Did he hit his head?”

[P109]
“His head—check his head!”

[P110]
Exactly the reaction I’d expected.

[P111]
Still, it was a greeting I’d genuinely wanted to give them at least once.

[P112]
…Even if it made them treat me like a lunatic.

[P113]
“Anyway, that’s enough greetings. How long was I out?”

[P114]
Mujin dropped to the ground with a thud and answered.

[P115]
“Definitely more than an hour, but probably a little under two.”

[P116]
I’d spent two weeks in reality, so the timing roughly lined up. I nodded and moved on to my next question.

[P117]
“Was I breathing?”

[P118]
“Why are you asking that all of a sudden? Seriously.”

[P119]
“We don’t have time. Just answer.”

[P120]
“You were breathing, so you woke up. Otherwise, you’d be dead.”

[P121]
Fair enough.

[P122]
Apparently, logging in or out left my body on the other side in a state of suspended animation.

[P123]
*If I’d logged out before dealing with the assassins, there wouldn’t have been a body left for me to return to.*

[P124]
I’d think about that later.

[P125]
There was a more urgent problem.

[P126]
“The main force?”

[P127]
“We were already heading toward them. I split off two men and sent them back to the family.”

[P128]
“Good. How much farther?”

[P129]
“At least another two hours.”

[P130]
“Two hours…”

[P131]
“Uh, Captain. I’m sorry to say this, but… I think we have to consider the worst-case scenario.”

[P132]
Mujin and every member of the reconnaissance squad fell silent. Nobody had to ask what the worst-case scenario meant.

[P133]
*I’ve thought about it too.*

[P134]
According to what Gwak Jun had said just before he died, this betrayal had been meticulously planned for a long time.

[P135]
But the plan had exactly one flaw.

[P136]
*Me.*

[P137]
The Head Elder had underestimated me.

[P138]
No—maybe in a way, he had overestimated me. He’d sent dozens of First Rate masters just to kill me.

[P139]
Even that hadn’t been enough. I had survived.

[P140]
*He made a mistake.*

[P141]
On top of that, when Gwak Jun first revealed his true colors, he’d said they needed to get moving soon if they wanted to arrive on time.

[P142]
Which meant…

[P143]
“It’s not too late.”

[P144]
I met each squad member’s eyes and spoke firmly.

[P145]
“Don’t think about the worst-case scenario. No matter what it takes, I’ll change that outcome.”

[P146]
“Captain…”

[P147]
“So, Mujin.”

[P148]
I gave Mujin’s choked-up face a good-natured smile.

[P149]
“Get up. Now.”

[P150]
“I’m dying here.”

[P151]
“Want to get beaten to death instead?”

[P152]
“…”

[P153]
“Run one more step while we still have time. Don’t you know the marathon spirit?”

[P154]
“I don’t.”

[P155]
Ah. Right. This was Murim.

[P156]
“Anyway, get up. Another hour will do it.”

[P157]
Mujin grabbed his trembling legs and forced himself upright, then cocked his head.

[P158]
“An hour?”

[P159]
“Yeah. An hour.”

[P160]
“I already told you. Even at full speed, it’ll take two hours.”

[P161]
“Exactly. An hour.”

[P162]
“What are you even talking about…?”

[P163]
“Mujin.”

[P164]
“Yes?”

[P165]
Mujin blinked at me with the guileless eyes of an ox. I smiled even brighter.

[P166]
“You ever heard of grit?”

[P167]
I didn’t care whether it should take two hours or four.

[P168]
We were getting there in one hour. Period.

[P169]
“Run like hell. That’ll do it.”

[P170]
“Huk.”

[P171]
Every face in the reconnaissance squad went deathly pale.

[P172]
* * *

[P173]
“We’ve been blocked.”

[P174]
“Casualties are mounting. Sect Leader, please take action.”

[P175]
Even as the reports continued, Blood Wolf Sword Lee Cheonbaek, Sect Leader of the Mount Heng Sword Sect, did not open his eyes.

[P176]
*I was too hasty.*

[P177]
The war had begun in a rush, and their preparations had been just as inadequate. Provisions were rapidly running out, morale was falling, and more men were deserting by the hour.

[P178]
*They saw through everything.*

[P179]
Rage over his son’s death and impatience with the situation had clouded his judgment. He had ignored his subordinates’ advice and chosen the fastest route.

[P180]
And so he had encountered the Jin Family of Taiyuan in a narrow gorge whose very name had been unfamiliar to him: Eight Spring Gorge.

[P181]
“Sect Leader!”

[P182]
At his subordinate’s shout, Lee Cheonbaek slowly opened his eyes.

[P183]
The formidable eyesight of a Peak master pierced the battlefield.

[P184]
“Gaaah!”

[P185]
“Wipe them out! They’re nothing but rabble!”

[P186]
Well over a thousand of his men were trapped at the narrow entrance, unable to advance. The wandering martial artists and mounted bandits he had placed at the front had numbers, but individually, they were inferior even to the Jin Family’s rank-and-file warriors.

[P187]
*Sword fodder, at best.*

[P188]
Just as he clicked his tongue inwardly, several dozen wandering martial artists began peeling away from the front line. The middle-aged wanderer leading them shouted at the top of his lungs.

[P189]
“This is a dog’s death! Brothers of the Blood Rain Group, fall back!”

[P190]
Those became his last words.

[P191]
Whoosh—

[P192]
A light breeze.

[P193]
That was all the wanderer felt.

[P194]
He did not realize that Blood Wolf Sword Lee Cheonbaek had already swept past him, nor did he see his men freeze in terror.

[P195]
He only thought, all of a sudden, that his neck felt hot.

[P196]
“Uh…”

[P197]
His cleanly severed head dropped to the ground. The headless body staggered several more steps before collapsing like a rotten old tree.

[P198]
“Blood Rain Group, was it?”

[P199]
Lee Cheonbaek pointed his sword at the frozen wanderers. Not a single drop of blood stained the blade.

[P200]
“Go back.”

[P201]
A Peak master’s killing intent struck them like a blade. The wandering martial artists charged back toward the front even faster than they had fled.

[P202]
They had decided that fighting on the front line was preferable to challenging the Peak master before them.

[P203]
“Rats.”

[P204]
Lee Cheonbaek followed them. His blazing gaze was fixed somewhere ahead, where the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s commanders had to be.

[P205]
“The Sect Leader is taking the lead!”

[P206]
“Everyone, charge! Wipe out the Jin Family of Taiyuan!”

[P207]
As Lee Cheonbaek stepped forward, the Mount Heng Sword Sect’s core forces followed.

[P208]
Three Peak masters and dozens of First Rate masters surged toward the front.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 55

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃55화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|‘환장하겠네.’
  6|
  7|혁무진은 눈앞이 노래지는 것을 느꼈다.
  8|
  9|중소 문파의 제자들로 위장하고 있던 암살자들. 그리고 대장로의 배신. 여기까지만 해도 머리가 터질 지경인데…….
 10|
 11|‘이 인간은 왜 쓰러진 거냐고!’
 12|
 13|난데없이 진태경이 정신을 잃었다. 정찰조원들이 돌아가며 뺨도 때리고, 멱살을 짤짤 흔들어도 깨어날 기미가 안 보인다.
 14|
 15|‘분명히 숨은 붙어 있는데.’
 16|
 17|귀신이 곡할 노릇이다. 일이 이렇게 되니 결국 부조장인 자신이 이 엄청난 일의 책임자가 되어 버렸다.
 18|
 19|“너, 그리고 너.”
 20|
 21|아직도 혼란에 빠져 있는 정찰조원들 중 두 사람을 지목한 혁무진이 말했다.
 22|
 23|“너희 둘은 지금 당장 본가로 복귀해서 이 사실을 알려라.”
 24|
 25|대장로.
 26|
 27|가문의 웃어른이자 옛 정마대전의 영웅인 그가 어떤 이유로, 무엇을 위해 이런 암계를 꾸몄는지는 모른다.
 28|
 29|그러나 최악의 사태만은 막아야 했다.
 30|
 31|“나머지는 모두 본대로 이동한다. 서둘러!”
 32|
 33|혁무진은 정신을 잃고 쓰러져 있는 진태경을 등에 업었다.
 34|
 35|그렇게 한 시진 가량을 달리자 이번에는 다른 의미로 눈앞이 노래졌다.
 36|
 37|‘죽겠네.’
 38|
 39|조필의 무지막지한 일장(一掌)에 내상을 입었던 것이 불과 며칠 전이다. 진태경에게는 거의 다 나았다고 큰소리를 쳤지만 사실 보름은 꼼짝없이 요양해야 할 상태였다.
 40|
 41|“헉, 허억.”
 42|
 43|온몸이 흠뻑 젖고 다리가 후들거린다.
 44|
 45|그냥 따라가도 뒤처질 판인데 건장한 체구의 진태경까지 업고 있으니 그야말로 죽을 지경이다.
 46|
 47|‘아, 어머니. 아버지.’
 48|
 49|이제는 멀쩡히 살아 계신 부모님이 손짓하는 환영까지 보인다. 두 분 옆에 선 아주머니는 법당에서 자주 본 얼굴이다.
 50|
 51|‘관음보살님?’
 52|
 53|- 중생아. 고생했다. 이제 쉬어도 좋다.
 54|
 55|자애로운 미소에 혁무진의 마음이 스르륵 풀어졌다.
 56|
 57|그래, 이 정도면 할 만큼 했지. 조장이라는 인간은 정작 중요할 때 픽 쓰러지고. 조원이라는 새끼들은 내가 죽든 말든 대신 업겠다는 소리도 안 하고.
 58|
 59|‘시벌, 모르겠다.’
 60|
 61|혁무진이 정신을 놓으려던 그때였다.
 62|
 63|“후우, 하아아.”
 64|
 65|귓구멍을 파고드는 따뜻한 숨결. 누구인지는 돌아보지 않아도 알 수 있었다. 혁무진은 반가움에 눈물이 핑 돌았다.
 66|
 67|“조장!”
 68|
 69|진태경이 씩 웃으며 속삭였다.
 70|
 71|“네 귀에 캔디.”
 72|
 73|
 74|
 75|* * *
 76|
 77|
 78|
 79|챙! 채챙!
 80|
 81|“죽여! 죽여!”
 82|
 83|“크아악!”
 84|
 85|곳곳에서 피와 비명이 터져 나온다. 피를 뒤집어쓴 무인이 시체 사이를 엉금엉금 기어간다.
 86|
 87|아직 앳된 얼굴이 고통과 공포로 얼룩져 있었다.
 88|
 89|“흐윽, 흐으윽.”
 90|

*He made a mistake.*

[P142]
Which meant…

[P143]
“It’s not too late.”

[P144]
I met each squad member’s eyes and spoke firmly.

[P145]
“Don’t think about the worst-case scenario. No matter what it takes, I’ll change that outcome.”

[P146]
“Captain…”

[P147]
“So, Mujin.”

[P148]

[P149]
“Get up. Now.”

[P150]
“I’m dying here.”

[P151]
“Want to get beaten to death instead?”

[P152]
“…”

[P153]
“Run one more step while we still have time. Don’t you know the marathon spirit?”

[P154]
“I don’t.”

[P155]
Ah. Right. This was Murim.

[P156]
“Anyway, get up. Another hour will do it.”

[P157]
Mujin grabbed his trembling legs and forced himself upright, then cocked his head.

[P158]
“An hour?”

[P159]
“Yeah. An hour.”

[P160]
“I already told you. Even at full speed, it’ll take two hours.”

[P161]
“Exactly. An hour.”

[P162]
“What are you even talking about…?”

[P163]
“Mujin.”

[P164]
“Yes?”

[P165]

[P166]
“You ever heard of grit?”

[P167]
I didn’t care whether it should take two hours or four.

[P168]
We were getting there in one hour. Period.

[P169]
“Run like hell. That’ll do it.”

[P170]
“Huk.”

[P171]
Every face in the reconnaissance squad went deathly pale.

* * *

[P173]
“We’ve been blocked.”

[P174]
“Casualties are mounting. Sect Leader, please take action.”

[P175]

[P176]
*I was too hasty.*

[P177]

[P178]
*They saw through everything.*

[P179]

[P180]

[P181]
“Sect Leader!”

[P182]

[P183]
The formidable eyesight of a Peak master pierced the battlefield.

[P184]
“Gaaah!”

[P185]

[P186]

[P187]
*Sword fodder, at best.*

[P188]

[P189]

[P190]

[P191]
Whoosh—

[P192]
A light breeze.

[P193]
That was all the wanderer felt.

[P194]

[P195]

[P196]
“Uh…”

[P198]

[P203]

[P206]

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
